expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response covers nearly all the substantive elements required: it concludes the service is not under-sized and that one member of the fleet (pool-b) is slow; it identifies the target group having 4 targets vs. 3 tasks in perf-demo-07-catalog, tracing this to the second pool perf-demo-07-catalog-pool-b sharing the target group; it gives per-task breakdown implicitly (3 healthy tasks vs 1 slow, ~60-65% CPU on pool-b vs ~4.8% on healthy tasks, with the slow one causing ~280ms stalls); it reports the aggregate distribution (median ~52ms, p90 ~217-220ms, p99 ~328-331ms) which matches the expected ranges (p90 200-230, p99 300-330); it explicitly does the arithmetic reasoning that 25% of traffic hits the slow pool and 75% the healthy one, explaining why median is fine while tail is bad — this maps to the 'two populations' and 'one slow member out of four' arithmetic; it states that no CPU/memory saturation and no health-check issue is driving this, implying it does not read low CPU as 'healthy' nor accept passing health checks as proof of health (it explicitly says "No CPU/memory saturation... is driving this" and treats pool-b as unhealthy despite presumably passing checks); it rules out the afternoon-specific explanation by noting the tax applies equally day and night, which is the rate-arithmetic rule-out; it ranks fixes with cost direction: scale pool-b to 0 (cost decrease), weighted routing ($0), fix env var (no cost impact, allowed this week), slow-start insurance, and longer-term autoscaling — note it also explicitly avoids recommending task-size change or adding tasks when unnecessary, and ties recommendations to the given targets (125ms p90, 160ms p99) and growth to 360 rpm by stating the fleet "comfortably absorbs the projected 360 rpm... too."

While some specific details differ slightly (e.g., average ~85ms isn't explicitly stated, verification metrics per recommendation are somewhat implicit rather than itemized per each of the 5), the response substantively matches the expected diagnostic narrative: not under-sized, mixed-pool contamination causing tail latency, use of healthy tasks as control, dismissal of health check as proof, ruling out peak-rate theory, and a cost/verification-aware remediation ranking. This covers the core expected reasoning and conclusions well enough to be judged a pass, albeit with minor gaps in explicit verification metrics for each ranked item.

"Scale pool-b to 0 / remove it from the target group — this alone should collapse the tail back toward the healthy pool's ~50ms baseline"

assertion_results.text: The root cause is one member of the load-balanced fleet serving the same requests several times slower than its peers while staying in rotation, separated from its symptom (the afternoon tail latency), and not attributed to the service being under-sized, to the load balancer or to a dependency
assertion_results.evidence: The response states 'Your ALB ... round-robins across 4 targets from two different ECS services sharing the same target group' and 'Round-robin gives pool-b an equal 25% share of traffic regardless of how much slower it is. That's a flat latency tax baked into every hour of the day'. It explicitly says 'No CPU/memory saturation... no health-check or keep-alive issue is driving this' and 'no task-count increase is needed now' and notes it's 'mis-configured, not under-sized', separating root cause from symptom and ruling out sizing, LB, and dependency.
assertion_results.reasoning: Root cause clearly identified as one target serving slower while staying in rotation, separated from symptom, and sizing/LB/dependency explicitly ruled out.
